title: Rainfall Field Reconstruction From Commercial Microwave Links via a Conditional Diffusion Model
content:
Abstract

High-resolution rainfall field reconstruction is a critical task in hydrological applications, with significant implications for flood forecasting, water resource management, and urban resilience. Conventional remote sensing instruments such as rain gauges and weather radars suffer from sparse coverage or high operational costs, while commercial microwave links (CMLs) provide a dense, low-cost, and opportunistic ground-based remote sensing network. However, deriving gridded rainfall fields from path-averaged CML attenuation constitutes an ill-posed inversion problem. To overcome this challenge, we propose CML-RainCDM, a physics-informed conditional diffusion framework that integrates link encoding, implicit spatial structure prior injection, and a forward rain attenuation constraint. By jointly leveraging spatial priors and physical consistency, the model achieves more accurate rainfall intensity estimation and improved preservation of fine-scale spatial structures compared with interpolation, statistical, and deep learning baselines. Sensitivity analyses further demonstrate its robustness in reconstructing heavy rainfall events, although extreme intensities remain difficult to capture. This study highlights the potential of opportunistic remote sensing via CMLs combined with generative diffusion models for practical, high-resolution precipitation monitoring and environmental remote sensing applications.
